about: A hold, an entry on one's own file, and the refusal sentences: what both resolvers (translator/src/resolver.ts and kernel/crates/resolver) must make of each program, from what this seat knows. Each case has `blocks` (the acts) or `asks` (the questions back, whole).

blocks.text: Please hold rec.44: nothing is to be done under it until this is withdrawn.

blocks.text: Please hold rec.44: nothing is to be done under it until this is withdrawn.

cases.name: whoever the call says is to hold it is taken as said, known record or not

blocks.text: Please hold rec.900: nothing is to be done under it until this is withdrawn.

cases.name: a record the seat has not seen addressed to anyone is not looked for
asks: You don't know of a standing paper called rec.900 that someone acts on. Look it up and name it by its id, or say who is to hold it.

cases.name: a notice addressed to nobody has nobody to hold it
asks: You don't know of a standing paper called rec.50 that someone acts on. Look it up and name it by its id, or say who is to hold it.

cases.name: an offer its maker has taken back cannot be signed
asks: rec.48 has been withdrawn: if it was an offer, whoever made it has taken it back, and there is nothing to sign.

cases.name: something withdrawn is not held
asks: rec.48 has been withdrawn: there is nothing to hold.

cases.name: what is addressed to one's own organisation is held on its own file, where its own people read it

blocks.text: Please hold rec.47: nothing is to be done under it until this is withdrawn.

cases.name: a hold is not also another kind of statement
asks: A hold says only what it holds, in what words, for whom and on what basis: nothing else should be written.

cases.name: something described and not named is no id
asks: You don't know of anyone or anything called "the wage payments" (for hold).

cases.name: acting as oneself, a hold is in one's own name (whether that person may hold it is for whoever acts on it)

blocks.text: Please hold rec.44: nothing is to be done under it until this is withdrawn.

cases.name: lifting a hold is withdrawing it
an entry on the organisation's own file is seen by it alone
cases.program: statement(kind=entry, visible=own, text="Tax withheld from the wages paid today, to be passed on at the month's end.", basis=rec.44)

blocks.text: Tax withheld from the wages paid today, to be passed on at the month's end.

cases.name: one's own file is one's own person's, acting as oneself
own is whoever the act is made for
cases.program: statement(kind=entry, visible=own, for=greenco, text="Kept for them.")

cases.name: own on any record that says who sees it
a request that needs something found out first is answered with one fixed sentence
asks: That needs something found out first. Look it up (in your own papers, or by asking whoever keeps it), then say what is to be done, naming each paper by its id.

cases.name: what nothing does: direct whoever sees to it
asks: Nothing here does that as such. If it is for someone else to see to, direct them in writing, on their form for it if they have one.

cases.name: a draft's name is not a paper on record: said so, with where its id is
asks: draft.finance.7 is the name a draft went by before it was confirmed, not a paper on record. Once confirmed it is on record under an id of its own (rec. and a number): look it up in your papers and name that.

cases.name: something written as an id that is none, where a letter answers a paper
cases.program: message(to=bank, text="Was the day-22 pay made?", re=rec.msg.4132)
asks: "rec.msg.4132" (for re) is not the id of anything on record: an id is written exactly as your papers show it, like rec.412. Look it up and name it so.

cases.name: and among the records an act cites
asks: "rec.msg.9" (for basis) is not the id of anything on record: an id is written exactly as your papers show it, like rec.412. Look it up and name it so.

cases.name: a paper is put up at a place on the ground, and a law's schedule is no place
cases.program: statement(kind=law, text="A landlord gives 90 days of notice.", on=schedule-tenancy, basis=rec.44)
asks: A paper is put up at a place on the ground: a lot, or a cell of one. schedule-tenancy is neither, as far as you know. To publish it and put it up nowhere, leave the place out; to put one paper in another's place, withdraw the other and publish this.

cases.name: an agreement with nothing on either side says nothing anyone commits to
cases.program: agreement(with=greenco, template=employment, text="Employment as works crew, paid by the finance office.", basis=rec.44)
asks: An agreement says what each side is to do or pay, and this one says nothing either side commits to. Say what you will do or pay, and what they will: money, goods, a building, occupancy, an account or work.
